results.denominator_free_potentials: Successive determinant coefficients give sigma=-t*theta-rho*y+k and z+t*w=k_t*y+k_rho*theta-y*theta+n. With r=k_rho, R=r-y, f=H2(k)+H1(n), the two later potentials are R*w+f(y,theta)=ell and f_V(y,theta)*w+H3(k)(y,theta)+H2(n)(y,theta)-ell_t*y-ell_rho*theta=m. Their derivation never divides by R.
results.zero_R_exclusion: If R vanishes identically then y is in L, z=A0-t*w, and constant J forces y_rho!=0. The explicit determinant is w_v*(y_t*A0_rho-y_rho*A0_t+y_rho*w), which has positive v-degree 2*deg(w)-1. This contradicts J0 in L*. Finite zeros of nonzero R are not excluded.
results.projected_quartic_bound: Eliminating w creates a polynomial H(U,V) of degree at most four. The exact identity R^2*J0=C_U*H_U(y,theta)+C_V*H_V(y,theta) proves H!=0. Its selected irreducible factor G occurs simply, and for H=GQ the evaluated cofactor Q(y,theta) divides R^2, with zeros confined to R=f_V=0. Rational recovery of w proves L(y,theta)=L(v); an elementary generic-linear-projection degree argument over exact L gives deg G=max(deg_v y,deg_v theta)<=4 without presuming a closed embedding.
results.vertex_free_cone_lemma: For any characteristic-zero field F, nonzero P and polynomials P,Q,S with PS=Q^2, F[P,Q,S]=F[v], unit ideal(P,Q,S), and max(deg P,deg Q)<=4 satisfy F[P,Q]=F[v]. Over an algebraic closure, coprime square factorization reduces to deg a=0,1,2; the quadratic case contradicts point separation and the linear case explicitly recovers the parameter. Faithful field-extension descent returns the conclusion to F.
results.whole_plane_generation: Set C=L[y,theta], O=L[v]=C[w]. A nonconstant projected polynomial makes O finite integral over C. Both R*w and f_V(y,theta)*w lie in C. For q(V)=f(r,V)-ell, the zero case directly returns w to C. In the nonzero squarefree case, Bezout yields 1=i0+i1*w with i0,i1 in (R,f_V)C; substituting this into a monic relation for w proves that ideal is the unit ideal in C, hence w lies in C.
results.repeated_center: The only remaining q is a nonzero repeated quadratic over L. Completing its square gives R*(w-D)=-kappa*(theta-theta0)^2. The actual constant determinant forbids the normalized triple from meeting the cone vertex. The quartic bound and full three-generator equality therefore satisfy the vertex-free cone lemma, proving L[y,theta]=L[v] also in this case.
